sentences.text:
Petitioners are seeking to quash the FIR and complaint in Crime No.98/2020 registered at Shanivarasanthe Police Station, Kodagu for the offences punishable under Section 498A, 181, 182,
200, 312, 323, 353, 465, 469, 500, 506, 509 read with 34 of IPC.
2.
The above case was registered on the basis of a private complaint filed by respondent No.2, which was referred to police for investigation.
3. The matter arises out of a matrimonial dispute.
Respondent No.2 is none other than the wife of petitioner NC: 2025:KHC:14965 No.1.
Petitioner Nos.2 to 4 are the parents and sister of petitioner No.1.

It is submitted that a complaint was also lodged by petitioner No.1 against respondent No.2,
which was registered in Crime No.13/2020 of the very same police station for offences punishable under Section 417, 504 and 506 read with 149 of IPC against respondent No.2 and others.

However,
B-report was filed in the said case.
4. Learned counsel appearing on both the sides would submit that the parties have settled the dispute and therefore, respondent No.2 is not interested in proceeding with the matter.
5. Learned counsel for respondent No.2 has filed a memo stating that the petition may be allowed and the criminal proceedings initiated against the petitioner may be quashed.
6. Memo filed by the learned counsel is placed on record.
The Hon'ble Apex Court in Narinder Singh and Others V. State of Punjab and Another reported in (2014) 6 SCC 466 has held

entities.text: Narinder Singh and Others V. State of Punjab and Another reported in (2014) 6 SCC 466
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
that when the parties have reached the settlement and on that basis,
petition for quashing the criminal proceedings is filed, the guiding factor in such cases would be:(i)
to secure the ends of justice; or (ii) to prevent abuse of the process of any Court.

Further, criminal cases having overwhelmingly and predominantly civil character, particularly those arising out of commercial transactions or arising out of matrimonial relationship or family disputes should be quashed when the parties have resolved their entire disputes among themselves.

8. In B.S.Joshi and others V. State of Haryana and another reported in (2003) 4 SCC 675, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has upheld the powers of the High Court under Section 482 of the code to quash criminal proceedings, where dispute is of a private nature and the compromise is entered into Sri Prashanth vs State Of Karnataka on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81088886/
3 between the parties.

sentences.text: In view of the settlement, no purpose will be served in continuing the proceedings pending against the petitioners.
Hence, to meet the ends of justice, it is necessary to quash the proceedings.

Accordingly, the following:
ORDER i. Petition is allowed.
ii. The FIR and complaint registered in Crime No.98/2020 of Shanivarasanthe Police Station, Kodagu and the consequent proceedings pending on the file of Court of Senior Civil Judge and JMFC Court, Somawarpet, Kodagu are quashed.
